text:
maria: quick heads-up — after upgrading otel-sdk from 1.3.0 -> 1.4.2 our background batcher is dropping child spans (~20% of traces). dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/traces?panel=worker-batcher :eyes:
ryan: which env and a sample trace id?
maria: prod-canary, trace id 4f9b3c2a7d8e9b1c
ryan: thx. can you check worker logs for that trace id (request-logs index) and paste the worker log around the request? also confirm runtime (python/Go/node)
maria: python 3.10, uvicorn + custom executor. log excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:45Z worker-1 INFO handling request id=4f9b3c2a7d8e9b1c
2026-03-17T09:12:45Z worker-1 DEBUG span:root-started trace=4f9b3c2a7d8e9b1c
2026-03-17T09:12:45Z worker-1 WARNING span:child-missing trace=4f9b3c2a7d8e9b1c reason="parent-context-not-found"
```
anita: that warning screams context propagation loss. did the upgrade change propagators or the tracerprovider init? any place we create new threads/processes or use ThreadPoolExecutor?
maria: we use concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor for the batcher and schedule tasks via loop.run_in_executor
anita: ThreadPoolExecutor + older opentelemetry versions sometimes relied on contextvars auto-propagation; newer SDK tightened behavior. quick check: print opentelemetry.trace.get_current_span() inside the task to see if context carries. you can also try forcing the propagator in init: 
```
from opentelemetry import trace, propagators
from opentelemetry.propagate import set_global_textmap
from opentelemetry.propagators.tracecontext import TraceContextTextMapPropagator

set_global_textmap(TraceContextTextMapPropagator())
# tracer provider setup...
```
ryan: also check your sampler — if sampling default changed, child spans may be dropped. what do you have set for OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER / TracerProvider sampler?
maria: env shows OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.1
anita: try a quick repro by setting sampler to always_on locally (or via env) to confirm it's sampling-related: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on. if spans come back, it's sampling. if not, it's propagation.
maria: ran a quick change in canary: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on — canary trace id 5a2c1b9f00011122 shows child spans again.
infra-bot: alert: trace-drop-rate spike detected on canary at 2026-03-17T09:10: - https://alerts.internal/trace-drop-canary
ryan: OK so sampling was part of it. but the warning "parent-context-not-found" suggests some tasks start without context and then parent-based sampling sees no parent and uses 0.1 rate -> drops children. two fixes: 1) ensure context propagation into executor tasks (use contextvars or wrap executor), 2) if you rely on remote parent, prefer parentbased_always_on_remote or force AlwaysOn for now.
anita: quick code patch we use in other services — wrapper to run tasks preserving context:
```
import contextvars
from functools import wraps

def preserve_context(fn):
    ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
    @wraps(fn)
    def inner(*a, **kw):
        return ctx.run(fn, *a, **kw)
    return inner

# usage: executor.submit(preserve_context(task_fn), ...)
```
maria: nice. i pushed a small canary PR that wraps batcher tasks with preserve_context and set sampler back to parentbased(0.1). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1289
ryan: can you also add a short test that simulates a traced parent scheduling a task into ThreadPoolExecutor and asserts child spans exist? helps catch regressions.
maria: will add test. quick deploybot:deploy started message if you need it
deploybot: deploy started: canary/batcher v2.6.3 -> sha abc123
maria: update — canary shows child spans stable for 30m after wrapper + revert sampler to parentbased. will roll to prod tomorrow during low traffic window. thanks @anita and @ryan :heart:
ryan: awesome. please add a note in the obs runbook about this upgrade caveat (sdk 1.4.x and thread executors). also link the PR in the runbook.
maria: will do. closing this thread for now.
